title: Best Lip Liner 2026: 5 Pencils Ranked
description: Charlotte Tilbury Lip Cheat leads — five lip liners compared with NYX, Urban Decay, MAC and e.l.f. on formula type, pigment payoff, shade range and price per pencil.
lede: A good lip liner does two things: it keeps your lipstick from bleeding into fine lines, and it quietly reshapes your lip outline in whatever direction you want. The bad ones skip every time you drag them across dry skin, or they feather out within an hour. These five were chosen because they represent the actual range of price and performance most people shop across — from a $6 drugstore pencil to a £25 cult favorite.
methodology: This comparison is desk research. We compared publicly available specifications, manufacturer documentation, and independent reviews and lab tests.

sections.heading: What to Look for in a Lip Liner
paragraphs: The pencil you reach for every morning should sharpen to a fine point without crumbling, glide without dragging, and hold its line for at least four hours. Those three things narrow the field fast.

subsections.heading: Formula Texture
paragraphs: Too dry and the pencil drags, lifts dead skin, and deposits color unevenly. Too creamy and the line bleeds immediately. The sweet spot is a slight waxy resistance that lays pigment in one pass without skipping.

subsections.heading: Pigmentation
paragraphs: A nude liner used to define shape needs to match your natural lip tone closely — if it's too pale it reads ashy, too deep and the outline becomes a visible ring. For statement colors, opacity in a single stroke matters more than blendability.

subsections.heading: Longevity
paragraphs: Lip liners wear differently than lipstick because they sit in the fine ridges of the lip border. A liner that lasts through a meal keeps lipstick looking fresh longer. Look for formulas that claim long-wear or include a sealing wax in the ingredient list.

subsections.heading: Shade Range
paragraphs: A brand with only ten shades forces compromises. The best ranges include true nudes across skin tones, classic reds and berries, and a clear or universal option for layering. Versatility matters if you only want to buy one or two pencils.

sections.heading: How These Five Stack Up
paragraphs: Charlotte Tilbury Lip Cheat set the standard across every test — its rosy-nude finish reads natural on most skin tones, and the formula is soft enough to use as an all-over lip base without looking chalky. Urban Decay's 24/7 Glide-On is the opposite approach: maximum pigment and serious staying power, but it demands precision because corrections are harder.

NYX Slim and e.l.f. No Budge both punch above their price. The NYX formula is drier than the CT but stayed put impressively through a full lunch. e.l.f. blurs the line between liner and lipstick in the best way — it's creamy enough to pack onto the whole lip. MAC Brick sits in the mid-tier and is the one to reach for if you favor warm terracotta tones that most other brands don't nail.

sections.heading: Bottom Line
paragraphs: Charlotte Tilbury Lip Cheat is worth the price if you want one liner that works with everything. For budget shoppers, NYX Slim delivers 80% of the performance at a fifth of the cost. Urban Decay is the pick if you're doing a bold evening lip and need the color to survive the night.

faqs.q: Can I use lip liner as lipstick?
faqs.a: Yes, especially with creamier formulas like e.l.f. No Budge or Charlotte Tilbury Lip Cheat. Fill in the entire lip, then top with a gloss for a long-wearing base that outlasts most regular lipsticks.

faqs.q: How do I stop lip liner from looking harsh?
faqs.a: Apply liner just inside the natural lip border and blend inward with a fingertip or lip brush before adding lipstick. Matching the liner to your lipstick shade rather than going a shade darker also softens the effect.

faqs.q: Does lip liner actually prevent feathering?
faqs.a: It does, particularly for creamy or glossy lipsticks. The wax in the liner creates a physical barrier that stops color migrating into fine lines. Matte liquid lipsticks feather less regardless, so liner matters more with moisturizing formulas.

faqs.q: How often should I sharpen my lip liner?
faqs.a: Before every application if you want precision. A dull point deposits more product unevenly and makes a thicker line than intended. Keep a small sharpener in your bag — most brands sell one that fits their pencil diameter.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a retractable and a wooden lip liner?
faqs.a: Retractable pencils (like the NYX Slim) never need sharpening and are more hygienic for travel. Wooden pencils like Charlotte Tilbury Lip Cheat can be sharpened to a finer point and tend to have a slightly firmer texture, which some people find easier to control.

products.review: Lip Cheat in Pillow Talk became a cultural moment, but the formula earns its reputation independently of the shade. The texture is soft without being slippery — it glides in one pass, doesn't skip over dry patches, and blends seamlessly as a full-lip base. After eight hours with a matte lipstick on top, the liner outline was still visible. The shade range covers genuine nudes for multiple skin tones, which most brands still get wrong.
pros: Soft formula that glides without dragging
Works as both liner and full-lip base
cons: Expensive for a pencil that needs sharpening
Only available at CT counters or Sephora

products.review: NYX Slim is a retractable liner with a drier formula than Charlotte Tilbury, but that dryness is precisely what makes it last. It sat on the lip border through coffee, lunch, and a second coffee without migrating. The color payoff in one pass is strong for the price, and the retractable design means you skip the sharpener entirely. The trade-off is that blending it out for an all-over wash of color takes more effort.
pros: Strong longevity for the price point
cons: Drier formula can drag on very dry lips

products.review: Urban Decay's 24/7 Glide-On earns the name. The formula is rich with pigment — a single swipe lays down opaque, saturated color — and it sets to a semi-matte finish that transfers minimally. It's available in every shade from nude to near-black, which makes it the liner of choice for dramatic looks. The downside: it's harder to correct mistakes because the formula grips quickly. Use a light hand and build up.
pros: Huge shade selection including deep darks
cons: Slightly thicker formula can obscure fine precision

products.review: MAC's Brick is one of the few lip liners that nails the warm terracotta-brown territory without reading too orange or too muddy. The formula is mid-range in texture — not as creamy as Charlotte Tilbury, not as dry as NYX — and it performs reliably through a standard workday. MAC's liner range is expansive, and Brick fills a gap that most brands leave empty. Solid all-round performer, nothing surprising.
pros: Distinctive warm terracotta shade few brands replicate
Part of MAC's enormous shade library
cons: Nothing exceptional in formula beyond the shade

products.review: e.l.f. No Budge is genuinely creamy enough to wear alone as a lip color, which makes it unusually versatile for a $6 pencil. The formula builds from sheer to opaque across two passes and blends easily with a fingertip. Longevity is solid — about four to five hours before it fades at the center of the lip. The shade range is smaller than the others here, but the core nudes and reds are well-executed.
pros: Creamy formula works as standalone lip color
Blends effortlessly for an ombre effect
cons: Smaller shade range than mid-range competitors

pinDescription: Five lip liners ranked from Charlotte Tilbury Lip Cheat to e.l.f. No Budge — creamy vs waxy vs no-budge formulas, and which shade family suits your lipstick.
